items.title: Add a signed satMutMPRA regulatory-effect ranking benchmark

labels.name: agent-generated
labels.description: Issue or pull request created by an AI agent

items.body:
## Summary

Add VEPBench's first quantitative ranking task using the 16 canonical
saturation-mutagenesis MPRA validation sets published with CADD v1.7. For each
regulatory element, a model receives the assay context, the complete reference
element sequence, and 50 compact GRCh38 VCF variants with statistically
significant assay effects. It predicts a signed log2 activity effect for every
variant.

The primary metric is Spearman rank correlation between predicted and measured
effects. Pearson correlation is reported as a secondary measure of whether the
spacing between predictions tracks experimental effect magnitude.

This issue is an explicit proposal to extend VEPBench beyond its current
multiple-choice, exact-match-only task contract. The implementation must add a
versioned ranking contract without changing the meaning of existing published
question or result records.

## Motivation

The current benchmark tasks classify individual variants. A quantitative
satMutMPRA task would instead test whether a general-purpose language model can
prioritize noncoding substitutions and single-base deletions with
experimentally supported effects according to their measured,
cell-context-specific regulatory activity.

The task is analogous to the listwise variant-effect evaluation used by
[ProteinGymLLM](https://www.proteingymllm.com/), but it asks for numerical
predictions so that both ordinal and cardinal agreement can be evaluated.

The source study measured promoter and enhancer activity at single-base
resolution:

- Kircher et al., [Saturation mutagenesis of twenty disease-associated
  regulatory elements at single base-pair
  resolution](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-11526-w)
- CADD v1.7 [paper](https://academic.oup.com/nar/article/52/D1/D1143/7511313)
  and [published RegSeq validation
  VCFs](https://kircherlab.bihealth.org/download/CADD-development/v1.7/validation/regseq/)
- [MaveDB REST API](https://api.mavedb.org/docs) and an example
  [F9 score set](https://www.mavedb.org/score-sets/urn:mavedb:00000015-a-1)

## Canonical task scope

Use exactly the following 16 CADD v1.7 validation files, one per regulatory
element:

1. `SatMut.all.F9.vcf.gz`
2. `SatMut.all.GP1BA.vcf.gz`
3. `SatMut.all.HBB.vcf.gz`
4. `SatMut.all.HBG1.vcf.gz`
5. `SatMut.all.HNF4A.vcf.gz`
6. `SatMut.all.IRF4.vcf.gz`
7. `SatMut.all.IRF6.vcf.gz`
8. `SatMut.all.LDLR.vcf.gz`
9. `SatMut.all.MSMB.vcf.gz`
10. `SatMut.all.MYCrs6983267.vcf.gz`
11. `SatMut.all.PKLR.vcf.gz`
12. `SatMut.all.SORT1.vcf.gz`
13. `SatMut.all.TCF7L2.vcf.gz`
14. `SatMut.all.TERT.vcf.gz`
15. `SatMut.all.ZFAND3.vcf.gz`
16. `SatMut.all.ZRSh13.vcf.gz`

Preserve the source identifiers in provenance. Resolve and document the
`GP1BA` source filename versus `GP1BB` biological-name discrepancy before
choosing the model-visible name.

Do not add other satMutMPRA elements, alternative cell conditions, flipped
constructs, or independent-library replicates in this version. The CADD file
selection is the canonical selection for this task.

## Source and provenance

Use the CADD validation VCFs as the authoritative source for:

- canonical element selection;
- GRCh38 VCF alleles, including normalized one-base deletions;
- the full-precision signed experimental effect in `INFO/EF`;
- the experimental p-value in `INFO/PV`;
- barcode support in `INFO/BC`; and
- the source `FILTER` classification.

Use MaveDB records as the structured source for target sequences and available
experiment metadata. Augment missing assay details from the original study or
its data portal when needed. Maintain an explicit crosswalk from every CADD
element to its MaveDB score-set URN and source-study element label.

Do not use rounded MaveDB score values as the ground truth when the
full-precision CADD value is available. Validate the crosswalk by matching
coordinates, alleles, rounded effects, and barcode counts. The legacy MaveDB
records must not be used naively for deletion notation: for example, the F9
record represents a source deletion as a target-equality expression, while the
CADD VCF contains its normalized deletion allele.

Record source URLs, retrieval dates, byte sizes, and cryptographic digests in a
provenance manifest. Commit only the compact deterministic task source needed
to reproduce generated questions; do not hand-edit generated artifacts.

## Variant eligibility filters

The source VCF `FILTER` labels are task-specific experimental QC categories:

| Filter | Interpretation | Count across 16 VCFs | Task treatment |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `SIGN` | At least 10 barcode tags and `PV < 1e-5` | 4,332 | Include |
| `MIN` | At least 10 barcode tags but not in `SIGN` | 17,685 | Exclude |
| `QUAL` | Insufficient barcode support; observed range 1-9 tags | 1,499 | Exclude |

The eligible pool is therefore the 4,332 records with `FILTER` equal to
`SIGN`. Include both substitutions and normalized one-base deletions. Do not
apply an additional filter on RNA counts, DNA counts, or effect magnitude.

This reproduces the CADD v1.7 RegSeq evaluation threshold: at least 10 barcode
tags and `PV < 1e-5`. Restricting the benchmark to statistically supported
effects avoids asking the model to finely rank a large group of uncertain,
near-zero measurements. It deliberately makes neutral-versus-functional
discrimination a separate future task.

Preserve `PV`, `BC`, and `FILTER` in private scoring provenance, but never
include them in the model-visible prompt. The generator must verify before
panel construction that every element contains at least 50 eligible records.

## Deterministic panel construction

Generate exactly one 50-variant panel for each of the 16 elements:

1. Filter the element to `SIGN` records.
2. Sort by signed `EF` ascending, with a documented stable VCF-key tiebreaker.
3. Divide the sorted records into ten equally populated rank-quantile bins,
   with bin sizes differing by at most one.
4. Deterministically select five records without replacement from each bin
   using a versioned seed and sampling procedure.
5. Combine the 50 selected records and deterministically shuffle their display
   order so effect quantile is not leaked.
6. Assign stable, opaque candidate IDs such as `V01` through `V50` after the
   display order is fixed.

The implementation must document and pin the seed. There are no repeated
draws or alternative panels in this version. Rebuilding from the same pinned
sources and configuration must produce byte-identical question JSONL and the
same manifest digest.

Ground-truth ties are allowed and must use average ranks when computing
Spearman correlation.

## Model-visible prompt

For each element, provide:

- gene or regulatory-element name;
- promoter or enhancer classification;
- cell line;
- MPRA assay description;
- transfection time and experimental treatment, where applicable;
- the full reference regulatory-element sequence in its validated orientation;
- genome assembly `GRCh38`; and
- the 50 candidates as a compact VCF table containing only `CHROM`, `POS`,
  `ID`, `REF`, and `ALT`.

Do not provide disease association, known functional variants, publication
title or DOI, measured wild-type fold change, `EF`, `PV`, `BC`, or the source
`FILTER` value.

The prompt must explain standard anchored VCF deletion representation. It
should request one predicted signed log2 activity effect per candidate:

- positive values mean increased reporter activity;
- negative values mean decreased reporter activity;
- zero means no predicted activity change; and
- numerical distances should represent predicted differences in effect
  magnitude, although exact calibration is not required.

Only the prompt crosses the provider boundary. Reference scores remain local.

## Output contract and parsing

Require a final line containing a strict JSON object keyed by candidate ID, for
example:

```text
FINAL: {"V01": -0.42, "V02": 0.08, "V03": 0.71}
```

The parser must:

- read only the last well-formed `FINAL: <json-object>` line;
- reject duplicate JSON keys rather than silently accepting the last value;
- require every expected candidate ID exactly once;
- reject missing or additional candidate IDs;
- accept only finite JSON numbers; and
- avoid heuristic recovery from prose or earlier output.

Do not impute missing candidate scores. A completed but invalid model response
receives `-1.0`, the floor of both correlation metrics, plus a parse error.
An API failure retains the existing null-score/incomplete-run semantics.
Report the valid-output rate separately. A valid constant prediction vector
has zero association for both metrics rather than an undefined value.

## Scoring and aggregation

For each element:

1. Join predictions to the 50 full-precision signed `EF` values by opaque ID.
2. Compute Spearman rank correlation using average ranks for ties.
3. Compute Pearson correlation on the numerical predictions and `EF` values.

The task-level metrics are the unweighted arithmetic means of the 16
element-level correlations:

- **Primary:** mean Spearman rho.
- **Secondary:** mean Pearson r.
- **Diagnostic:** valid-output rate.

Do not pool variants across elements before calculating correlation, because
experimental and predicted numerical scales may differ between prompts. Do
not combine Pearson and Spearman into a composite score.

The ranking task should initially have a task-specific leaderboard. Defining a
heterogeneous overall score that combines correlation with the existing
classification accuracies is outside this issue.

## Public contract and implementation impact

The current public schemas only support `task_type: multiple_choice` and
`metric: exact_match`. Add a versioned ranking question/result contract that
preserves validation of existing v1 records. The new structured question must
contain enough information to validate and score the candidate set without
parsing the rendered prompt.

Update, as needed:

- deterministic source preparation and validation;
- question and result schemas;
- prompt rendering and cross-field invariants;
- strict final-answer parsing;
- per-question scoring;
- run aggregation and publication schemas;
- the static task leaderboard and question explorer; and
- contributor and task methodology documentation.

Continue to preserve the complete provider response, final content, nullable
provider-exposed reasoning, usage, finish reason, non-secret request
parameters, complete generated question, and all existing question-set
fingerprints in local results.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The task uses exactly the 16 published CADD v1.7 RegSeq validation VCFs
      listed above.
- [ ] Every CADD element has a documented MaveDB/source-study metadata
      crosswalk and a validated reference sequence orientation.
- [ ] The compact prepared source and its provenance manifest validate all VCF
      reference alleles and normalized deletions against GRCh38.
- [ ] Eligibility is exactly `FILTER == SIGN`; all `MIN` and `QUAL` rows are
      excluded.
- [ ] The prepared eligible population contains 4,332 variants, subject to
      verification against the pinned upstream file digests.
- [ ] Every element has at least 50 eligible variants; preparation fails with
      a clear error if this invariant is not met.
- [ ] Generation produces exactly 16 questions with exactly 50 candidates per
      question and exactly five candidates from each signed-effect quantile.
- [ ] Candidate display order and IDs do not expose source order, score order,
      significance, barcode support, or effect values.
- [ ] The model-visible prompt contains the agreed experimental context, full
      reference sequence, and compact GRCh38 VCF candidates.
- [ ] The model-visible prompt excludes every ground-truth and QC field.
- [ ] The strict parser rejects missing, extra, duplicate, nonnumeric, and
      nonfinite predictions without heuristic recovery.
- [ ] Scoring has offline tests for perfect, reversed, tied, constant, invalid,
      and partially missing predictions.
- [ ] Spearman is the primary task metric; Pearson and valid-output rate are
      published separately.
- [ ] Task aggregation is an equal-weight mean across the 16 elements.
- [ ] Existing multiple-choice question and result records remain valid and
      retain their existing scoring behavior.
- [ ] Task methodology and shared architecture/evaluation/publication
      documentation are updated in the same change.
- [ ] Tests make no live MaveDB, CADD, or model API calls.
- [ ] `uv run --locked pytest` and `uv run --locked ruff check .` pass.

## Out of scope

- Additional satMutMPRA elements or alternative assay conditions.
- Multiple independently sampled panels per element.
- Ranking non-significant or near-neutral measurements, or classifying variants
  as neutral versus functional.
- Restriction to SNVs.
- Model access to external tools, annotations, alignments, or genomic browsers.
- MAE or RMSE as leaderboard metrics.
- Combining ranking correlations with classification accuracy in the existing
  all-task aggregate.
- Any database, backend service, authentication, or submission system.

## Methodological limitations to document

- The benchmark uses one public, historical study and is a development set,
  not a contamination-resistant hidden test.
- One deterministic N=50 panel per element is sensitive to the selected
  variants; repeated panels can be considered in a later version.
- Quantile-stratified sampling guarantees representation from every empirical
  effect decile, but metric values remain specific to the selected finite
  panel.
- Conditioning on `PV < 1e-5` limits the task to statistically detectable
  effects. Statistical significance depends on assay power and is neither
  proof of biological importance nor evidence that every excluded variant is
  truly neutral.
- The 10-tag minimum and significance filter reduce measurement noise but do
  not eliminate it, particularly for less frequently generated deletion
  alleles.
- Pearson correlation is more sensitive than Spearman correlation to outliers
  and nonlinear score transformations.
- MPRA reporter activity is an experimental molecular phenotype and should not
  be interpreted directly as organismal pathogenicity.

## Alternatives considered

- **All portal elements versus the CADD subset:** Using every satMutMPRA
  element and condition would provide broader coverage, but would require
  decisions about alternate conditions and replicate-like source records. The
  first version instead uses the 16 validation VCFs selected and distributed
  with CADD v1.7.
- **MaveDB scores versus CADD VCF effects:** MaveDB is useful for learning the
  API and obtaining structured sequence and experiment metadata, but its
  legacy scores are rounded and at least one deletion representation requires
  special handling. The CADD VCFs therefore provide the canonical alleles and
  full-precision effects; MaveDB remains a metadata source and cross-check.
- **All barcode-qualified variants versus significant variants only:** Keeping
  both `MIN` and `SIGN` would yield 22,017 variants and test a more natural mix
  of effects. However, only about 20% are `SIGN`, so a typical 50-variant panel
  would contain many uncertain near-zero measurements whose fine-grained
  ordering may largely reflect assay noise. This version uses the 4,332
  `SIGN` variants and leaves neutral-versus-functional prediction to a future
  task.
- **SNVs only versus all supported allele types:** Restricting to SNVs would
  simplify representation, but would discard measured one-base deletions and
  diverge from the CADD evaluation. Both substitutions and normalized
  one-base deletions are retained.
- **Panels of 10 or 30 versus 50 variants:** Smaller panels would reduce prompt
  length and generation cost, but provide a less stable correlation estimate
  and less coverage of the effect range. Fifty is still practical with only
  16 prompts per model and is consistent with ProteinGymLLM's primary panel
  size.
- **Unstratified random sampling versus effect-stratified sampling:** A simple
  random sample could overrepresent a narrow portion of an element's measured
  range. Stratifying on the private ground truth guarantees coverage across
  the rank distribution without revealing that information in the prompt.
- **Equal-width effect bins versus equal-population quantile bins:** Equal-width
  bins preserve fixed numerical intervals, but skewed distributions and
  outliers can create sparse or empty bins and force disproportionate sampling
  of rare extremes. Ten deterministic equal-population rank bins guarantee
  enough candidates for five samples per bin.
- **Three independent draws versus one fixed panel:** Repeated draws would
  quantify sampling sensitivity, as in ProteinGymLLM, but triple evaluation
  cost and add another aggregation layer. The first version uses one
  deterministic panel per element and documents panel sensitivity as a
  limitation.
- **An ordered list versus one numerical score per variant:** A rank-only
  response would directly support Spearman correlation and be easier to
  interpret. Numerical signed predictions additionally encode direction and
  relative magnitude, enabling Pearson correlation while still permitting
  Spearman scoring.
- **Treating missing predictions as zero versus strict rejection:** Imputing
  zero would reward omission and conflate failure to provide a prediction with
  a substantive prediction of neutral activity. Responses must contain one
  finite score for every candidate; incomplete mappings are invalid.
- **Spearman alone versus Spearman plus Pearson:** Spearman is retained as the
  primary metric for ranking quality. Pearson is reported separately as a
  secondary measure of effect-spacing agreement, with no composite of the two.
- **Pooling all variants versus scoring within elements:** A pooled correlation
  would mix assays and model outputs whose numerical scales can differ by
  element. Correlations are computed within each element and then averaged
  with equal element weight so large elements do not dominate.
- **Full mutant sequences or local sequence windows versus compact VCF rows:**
  Repeating 50 mutated sequences would greatly increase prompt size, while
  local windows would duplicate information already recoverable from the full
  reference element. The prompt includes the reference sequence once and
  represents candidates as compact `CHROM POS ID REF ALT` rows.

items.title: Unify variant eligibility and evaluate score-based panel sampling

labels.name: agent-generated

items.body:
Replace consequence/SNV restrictions and rank-quantile sampling with one reproducible task-construction protocol that admits complete, experimentally measured alleles and samples across effect magnitude.

## Status and durable handoff — 2026-09-09

**The protocol rollout is complete.** [PR #64](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/pull/64) merged on 2026-09-08 at `bf22715df534977066229c01cc8c5fee6d8baee7`. All 52 version-2 questions were regenerated and verified. All 18 runs (312 responses: Luna, Sol and Astra at medium/high reasoning) completed with valid outputs and zero API errors. DeepSeek was excluded as requested. Total evaluation cost was **$28.1459108**.

Questions and complete result artifacts are published to the Hugging Face bucket as [named version `protocol-v2-20260908`](https://huggingface.co/buckets/open-athena/VEP-bench/resolve/versions/protocol-v2-20260908/manifest.json) and promoted to official `versions/main`. The [results explorer](https://openathena.ai/VEP-bench/) is live; its manifest/run index match the validated local publication. The exact [post-publication canary](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/actions/runs/34315657249) passed on 2026-09-09. [Final scores and verification](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/issues/62#issuecomment-5602305090) are recorded below. No further model runs or HF publication are needed for this closeout.

Analysis is preserved separately on **`codex/issue-62-sampling-analysis`** and must not merge into `main`:

- [Preliminary full-population report](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/blob/e9f628557e1776726b703f1c3077ad16a73099c2/docs/analysis/task-sampling-2026-09-04.md): methods, pins, plots, occupancy tables, windows and exclusions. [Analysis PR #63](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/pull/63) remains closed without merging.
- [MPRA v1-to-v2 diagnostic report](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/blob/7e034d77417c156be9f39f5f9d2a148429f08b79/docs/analysis/mpra-v1-v2-2026-09-08.md): interpretation of the existing Sol medium results, with [archived inputs and panel metrics](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/tree/7e034d77417c156be9f39f5f9d2a148429f08b79/docs/analysis/mpra-v1-v2-2026-09-08) and an [offline verifier](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/blob/7e034d77417c156be9f39f5f9d2a148429f08b79/scripts/verify_mpra_comparison.py). The 1,600 archived candidate records reproduce the panel/subset metrics and summaries to 1e-12. The archive does not depend on the former mutable HF `main` publication remaining available. **Retain the branch.**

One repository follow-up is open: [PR #65](https://github.com/Open-Athena/VEP-bench/pull/65) adds only the two Astra model profiles and the reviewed catalog metadata already used in publication. It contains no analysis or benchmark changes. The new configs match all six published Astra runs; 14 profile/catalog tests and Ruff passed locally.

The user authorized and delegated SkyPilot operation, then authorized merge, evaluations and publication. Preparation workers were terminated. The one-off rollout services were disabled after completion. Operational receipts remain in `.vepbench/rollout-20260908/` in `/home/exedev/.codex/worktrees/fef6/VEP-bench`; the durable public analysis, generated questions and results are linked above. Earlier comments describing pending execution/publication are superseded by this status.

## User decisions and scope

- Remove all SGE consequence filtering, precomputed consequence joins, GTF nearest-exon reclassification, missense/splicing balancing, class-based window preferences, and **both SNV restriction and SNV preference**. Keep primary experimental MaveDB scores.
- Apply the same eligibility principle across all datasets: retain complete validated alleles, including substitutions, insertions, deletions, duplications, and multibase replacements when present. No variant-type quota or arbitrary length cutoff. Do not split one assayed multibase allele into separately scored variants or invent measurements.
- MPRA uses **SIGN + MIN**, with **QUAL excluded**. MIN is barcode-qualified measurement; nonsignificance is neither failed QC nor proof of neutrality.
- Revisit OpenSplice's windows on the expanded population. The previous 20 are a comparison baseline, not a selection constraint.
- **Latest explicit cleanup decision: remove AlphaGenome complexity entirely for now.** Do not retain prediction baselines, missing-prediction tracking, prediction joins, auxiliary input downloads, configuration, provenance requirements, or tests. This supersedes the initial proposal to retain missing baselines explicitly.
- Remove obsolete implementation, cache compatibility paths, dependencies, tests, and documentation. Saved model evaluations remain pinned to their original question sets; “historical results” refers only to those existing snapshots, not a requirement to retain old preparation logic or analysis files on main.
- Implement the protocol in a separate PR against main. The user subsequently authorized its merge, fresh evaluations and publication; those steps are complete as recorded above.

The original motivation was to cover effect magnitudes more meaningfully than equal-population quantiles, with five bins and ten variants per bin as the initial target. The full-population audit established the endpoint and sparse-bin rules below.

## Final shared protocol

1. Apply source-specific measurement QC, validate full reference sequences and coordinate mappings, and resolve allele identities before calculating sampling populations. Keep every measured allele intact. Exclude ambiguous equivalent identities rather than choosing one conflicting measurement. OpenSplice's already-unique master fails closed if duplicate constructs or conflicting gene assignments appear.
2. Retain native signed scores: reviewed damage-direction sign only for SGE, signed delta PSI for OpenSplice, signed log2 reporter-activity effects for MPRA. Do not use absolute values, cross-assay normalization, clipping, or rescaling.
3. For each eligible assay/window, compute **P01/P99 using Hyndman–Fan type 7**, then place four equally spaced internal cutpoints in score units. This defines five score-space bins, not equal-population bins. Values below P01 and above P99 remain in the outer bins with unchanged labels. Cutpoint equality goes right; equal scores are never split across bins.
4. Select **50 unique candidates**. Allocate evenly up to each bin's capacity; take all alleles in sparse bins and redistribute remaining slots evenly across bins with capacity. Ascending bin index resolves remainder ties. Example: capacities `[400, 80, 12, 6, 2]` yield `[15, 15, 12, 6, 2]`. Empty intermediate bins are allowed. Do not move/merge boundaries or drop assays merely to force exactly 5×10.
5. Reject populations below 50 or with collapsed P01/P99 anchors explicitly. There is no min/max or rank-quantile fallback. None of the selected production windows has collapsed anchors.
6. Within each bin, sort by SHA-256 of compact UTF-8 JSON `[seed, question_key, zero_based_bin_index, allele_key]`, then stable allele key. Seed is `2026090400`; algorithm is `sha256_score_space_v1`. Sort selected normalized display alleles by local position, REF, ALT before assigning opaque `V01`–`V50` IDs.
7. Retain anchors, cutpoints, interpolation/boundary/tail conventions, population counts, allocations, algorithm, seed, selected identities/digests, QC, and exact source identities in private provenance. Keep measured scores, bins, QC, native coordinates and identifiers out of candidate prompts. No unrelated prompt-context or scoring change is requested.

For window selection, maximize full-population **P95−P05**, breaking ties by larger eligible count and ascending exon identity. SGE selects one window per reviewed gene. OpenSplice first selects one exon per gene, then the top 20 gene winners; cross-gene ties use count, gene, exon ID. Do not preserve an SNV/class preference indirectly through window selection.

## Source-specific implementation decisions

**SGE:** complete REF validation uses pinned GRCh38, with declared cdot transcript geometry and reviewed DDX3X/TINF2 MANE fallbacks. TINF2 target `n.` coordinates are mapped as CDS coordinates only after exact target/CDS identity. Transcript and genomic HGVS support substitutions, delins, deletions, insertions, and duplications on both strands. Exon windows retain exactly 100 bp on each side; the entire normalized REF span must fit. Reverse-strand display uses the full REF span and reverse-complements both alleles. Explicit source REF mismatches are rejected, never silently repaired or swapped. All rows belonging to duplicated normalized alleles are excluded.

Include **CARD11 baseline `urn:mavedb:00001226-a-1`**, declared target `ENST00000396946.9`: endogenous diploid TMD8 growth assay without ibrutinib, damage direction −1. It has 3,842 unique validated alleles after excluding two duplicate rows; its selected window has 1,006. This produces 16 SGE questions, not additional questions for other CARD11 conditions. Its pinned metadata links [PMID 33202260](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33202260/), electronically published 2020-11-16; the explorer date follows that indexed record.

**OpenSplice:** use Figshare v5 experimental master plus wild-type exon metadata. Require measured status, finite delta PSI, three finite replicate PSI values, usable identities, and complete mutant-sequence reconstruction. Normalize RNA U to DNA T. Deposited substitutions and `∆Nnt` deletions retain their entire assayed edit; deletion markers must match length. The complete display cassette remains `FAS exon 5 + FAS intron 5 + wt_seq + FAS intron 6 + FAS exon 7`, with actual source-derived upstream flank lengths (including the four short-flank exons), not a blanket 70-nt assumption.

Exon geometry comes from wild-type exon metadata. Ignore the master table's per-variant `exon_length`: it is inconsistent for some valid deletions. For example, `CD46_e7_del100to120` removes 16 bases from a 45-base exon based on its coordinates and complete mutant sequence, while that annotation says 28 remain. Exact whole-mutant reconstruction is the validation criterion. Predictor-derived genomic POS/alleles and AlphaGenome inputs are no longer needed for the construct-relative VCF. Keep `opensplice_snv` as the existing task-family/package/path identifier; human-facing wording describes variants, and changed questions use a new template identity.

**MPRA:** retain all 23,516 source records for CADD/MaveDB crosswalk and genomic-reference validation; source QC yields 22,017 SIGN+MIN records. Normalize alleles against the complete reporter insert and exclude all rows sharing a normalized allele identity before sampling. This removes 146 equivalent rows, leaving 21,871 eligible alleles. Genomic VCF padding outside the displayed insert may be removed only after upstream validation, then re-anchored inside the display; whole edits must remain equivalent. Preserve construct orientation and fixed reporter context. The exact ZRS terminal reference-discrepancy exception remains limited to the pinned excluded QUAL row; no general mismatch allowance was introduced.

## Evidence and regenerated results

The old protocol had 15 SGE questions from 55,924 consequence-filtered SNVs, OpenSplice sampled from 300,327 eligible SNVs, and MPRA sampled only 4,332 SIGN rows. The audit compared min/max and P01/P99 endpoints on full expanded populations, separately from old-window comparisons. Its full methodology and limitations remain in the pinned report above.

Production results:

| Task | Eligible population | Questions | Selected allele types | Exact 5×10 panels |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| SGE | 118,834 before windows | 16 | 487 SNVs, 116 multibase substitutions, 180 deletions, 17 insertions | 13/16 |
| OpenSplice | 578,611 across 586 eligible exons and 458 genes | 20 | 410 SNVs, 590 deletions | 7/20 |
| MPRA | 21,871 after QC and normalized-identity exclusion | 16 | 740 SNVs, 60 deletions | 16/16 |

All **52 panels contain 50 unique sequence-valid candidates: 2,600 total, including 963 non-SNVs**. OpenSplice changes 18/20 windows; one additional exon has only 35 eligible variants. SGE changes 6/15 previous windows and adds CARD11. Twelve SGE source rows across DDX3X, RAD51C and CARD11 belong to duplicate identities; there are no mapping failures in the pinned included sets. MPRA's post-normalization count is the production refinement of the audit's 22,017 source-QC count.

Source SHA-256 values from the generators:

- SGE: `72d6bc847f0bc799e8846fc63f1129844eb0bf554092dc01f81f8471c959547c`
- OpenSplice: `7956ccc156f05b832ffe89e1dc4f0cf6471ae05bfe55d0b82d237f3ad3c953a8`
- MPRA: `550882be248605a5505be40519e97569d45f1431bd6ea5fb234039499429ae21`

These panels deliberately change the prediction population. Broader score separation can improve correlation without improving ordering within effect groups. Keep within-question Spearman as primary, Pearson and valid-output rate as secondary; do not interpret changed scores as directly comparable improvement over older question sets. No new metric, statistical framework, or hidden-test infrastructure was introduced; evaluations were subsequently authorized and completed.

## Code map, versioning, and validation

## Independent review and follow-up

Independent review of PR #64 completed after the initial implementation. One P2 finding was confirmed: OpenSplice private source REF/ALT used the normalized VCF anchor position, so 590 deletion provenance tuples did not reconstruct the assayed cassette. Public VCF alleles and measured scores were correct. The fix records the original cassette edit position and adds reconstruction assertions for the source insert, private cassette edit, and public VCF across all four deletion lengths.

The review also identified an obsolete MPRA VCF parser restriction to SNVs and one-base deletions. No pinned rows were excluded by it, but it conflicted with the agreed cleanup and was removed. Regression fixtures cover multibase substitutions, insertions, longer deletions, replacements, and right-anchored first-base deletions while preserving full REF checks.

The reviewer independently checked 39,766 small complete edits for equivalent normalization/idempotence and 2,990 genomic HGVS deletions/replacements against expected mutant sequences. No other confirmed findings were reported. A follow-up review of both fixes and regression tests found the issues resolved. OpenSplice and MPRA artifacts/cache identities were regenerated from the pinned sources after the fixes; the selected panels and public candidate scores remain unchanged.

Post-fix validation: all 1,000 private OpenSplice cassette edits reconstruct exactly; public alleles, scores, and panel selection are unchanged. All 237 offline tests, Ruff, mypy, and pre-commit checks pass. Both fixes received follow-up independent review. The additional rebuild worker was terminated.
